newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund future's advance hit by strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Bund future's advance hit by strong U.S. data.

text.p: Bund futures slumped in late trade on Monday as a strong U.S. economic data including the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index and home sales hit global bond markets.
Traders said they expected Bunds to have a hard time quickly recovering from the late decline with the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday to ponder U.S. interest rates.
At 1456 GMT, the DTB September Bund futures contract was down 31 basis points at 101.54, after having traded in a range between 101.47 and 101.99.

Traders said contract support at 101.55 appeared strong enough to prevent further declines, but added the contract's inability to crack what is increasingly looking like strong resistance at 102.00 appears to be capping the topside.
From a fundamental standpoint, Bunds should continue to benefit from doubts about monetary union.

Edmund Stoiber, an influential member of the conservative Christian Social Union (SCU), has threatened to block German membership in monetary union in the upper house of parliament unless Maastricht Treaty criteria are strictly met.
Despite the fall in Treasuries, the spread between Bunds and their U.S. counterparts remained steady at around 89 basis points.
The spread against Italian debt narrowed to 114 basis points from 121 basis points as the market drew encouragement from the Bank of Italy's interest rate cut on Friday.

Domestically, analysts said demand for the government's 30-year bond could be slow because of memories of the last issue in 1994 that did not do well and because of fears that Bonn will not continue to issue the long-dated paper. Bonn will issue the debt on Tuesday and Wednesday.
